The memory used in a phone is different than the kind used in a flash drive.

RAM and internal memory is going to be written and rewritten many times per minute, which means it must be NAND flash, a type of memory that can be written almost infinitely without breaking down.

In comparison, flash drives use a cheaper and higher density type of memory that has a limited number of read / write cycles before it starts to degrade. This is because a storage drive will be used much less - you might write and modify the data on it only a dozen times per day, maximum.

It also doesn't help that manufacturers see cloud storage as a way to offload the memory requirements from their device to a service like Google, who is happy to give them kickbacks for including them on the phone by default. As a manufacturer that's a win-win!
